text:
Anita: Quick heads-up — partner onboarding hit a snag. SDKs/CLI disagree on env var names. Node samples reference REDWOOD_KEY, Python quickstart uses REDWOOD_TOKEN, CLI examples set REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT. Messy.

Ben: Oof. Do we have an official canonical list anywhere? If not we should pick one and stick to it.

Sam: Not formalized. Proposal from me: precedence order = 1) explicit key passed to client, 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT, 3) REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG, 4) REDWOOD_API_KEY (legacy). Use identical names across SDKs/CLI.

Anita: That ordering seems reasonable. Two runtime concerns: 1) how do we behave on key rotation (env var changes) and 2) how to avoid noisy retry storms when multiple processes see 401.

Ben: Runtime note: CLI is stateless so it should always re-read env at invocation. SDKs are long-lived — can't constantly watch file system. My suggestion: SDKs should read env on client construction; on first 401 response, re-read env once and retry the single request. If that still fails, surface an auth error. No persistent watcher.

Sam: Agreed. Pseudocode for SDKs (Node):
```js
// resolution order
const key = explicitKey || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
// send request
// if 401: re-read env, recompute key, retry once
```
And Python equivalent:
```py
key = explicit_key or os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT") or os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG") or os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
# on 401: key = re-read env, retry once
```

QA: Please add a short migration snippet for CI and Docker to the quickstart. Example GH Actions: `env: REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT }}`. Dockerfile should document `ARG` vs `ENV` warning for secrets.

Anita: Also we should avoid printing key values in logs. Instead log which env var name was used (e.g., "using REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT"). Add a clear deprecation message when REDWOOD_API_KEY (legacy global) is present along with a project-level key.

Ben: Ops/security: when a 401 triggers the SDK re-read+retry flow we should emit a metric `auth.retry_on_401` with tags for sdk_language and project_id (if available) so we can monitor rotation events.

Sam: I'll include a small example in the RFC showing how to implement metric emission and backoff policy (single immediate retry only). Longer retry loops are dangerous.

infra-bot: Created ticket DX-4240 "Standardize auth env vars + SDK 401 retry behavior" and linked to this thread.

Anita: Action items:
- @Sam: RFC with code snippets for Node/Python/Go, and grep results across repos for legacy var names (due Fri)
- @Ben: CLI PR to read unified env names + `redwood auth check` UX and deprecation warnings (start today)
- @Anita: update quickstart and all examples in docs + add CI/Docker snippets (WIP)
- @QA: test plan for rotation scenarios (staged env var swap, 401 path coverage)

Sam: One more thought: add a tiny helper in each SDK `resolveApiKey()` export so apps can reuse consistent behavior instead of copying logic. That'll keep samples concise.

Ben: Love that. Keep helper API stable and documented.

Anita: Thanks all. I'll ping infra/security after RFC for KMS/HSM rotation guidance and any signing constraints. :thumbsup:
